text:
mira: Heads-up — DAST in staging reported an endpoint returning what looks like a wrapped private key (base64 blob). I uploaded the raw response to ticket SEC-1247. Can someone confirm whether this is a test fixture or a real keystore leak?

jamal: I saw the upload, thanks. quick question — did the DAST runner include any auth headers? that helps know if it crawled an unauth endpoint or used a service account.

olga: pinging @alex (infra oncall) — did we change any KMS IAM bindings or RBAC for the staging batch jobs this morning?

alex: I rolled an IAM binding at 12:05 UTC for the staging batch-runner. changed role from roles/keystore.reader -> roles/keystore.decrypter to allow snapshot jobs. Only applied to staging project, not prod.

mira: do NOT restart the pod or cleanup the artifact. preserve everything. can you paste the exact binding diff here? we need to preserve chain of custody.

alex: diff: ```
- members: serviceAccount:batch-runner@staging.iam.gserviceaccount.com
- role: roles/keystore.reader
+ members: serviceAccount:batch-runner@staging.iam.gserviceaccount.com
+ role: roles/keystore.decrypter
```

sec-bot: KMS alert: Deny event logged for project-staging at 2024-06-30T12:07:34Z — requester: serviceAccount:batch-runner@staging.iam.gserviceaccount.com — method: AsymmetricDecrypt — status: PERMISSION_DENIED. (log id: projects/staging/logs/kms_20240630T120734) :warning:

jamal: that deny suggests someone tried to decrypt but lacked permission. DAST could have crawled an endpoint that simply echoed a cached encoded blob (fixture). not necessarily KMS compromise.

olga: steps we should take: snapshot the pod filesystem, copy S3 artifacts that the app uses, and export IAM/KMS audit logs for the last 24h. preserve sha256 for every artifact.

mira: i've halted new staging deploys and added label "security-investigation" to the service. ticket SEC-1247 has raw response body + curl command I used. do not rotate keys until we've confirmed scope.

alex: starting forensic copy now: `kubectl cp staging/app-pod:/var/app/cache /tmp/staging-evidence-$(date +%s)` then `aws s3 cp /tmp/staging-evidence-*.tar s3://redwood-incidents/SEC-1247/`. granting sec-eng ephemeral access TTL=1h.

jamal: when you upload, redact or replace long private key bytes in screenshots. use `openssl rsa -in suspect.key -text -noout` to confirm header vs full key. if it's a known test fixture, we'll file as FP and add a suppression fingerprint for the SAST/DAST runs.

olga: who owns the SAST rule set? @mira do you want a PR to add an allowlist entry for this fixture fingerprint with clear rationale and link to SEC-1247? we'll include a note to re-run baseline eval once suppression is added.

mira: yes, but only after we confirm — timeline: updates every 30m. if artifacts show actual private material from a keystore, we escalate to Compliance and rotate affected keys.

keystore-bot: Incident SEC-1247 created and assigned to sec-eng. Runbook: step1=evidence uploaded, step2=forensic snapshot in progress, step3=collect KMS/IAM audit logs.

mira: thanks — i'll post artifact hashes (sha256) and the KMS audit export when available. keep this channel as the single source of truth for the next 2 hours. if anyone opens a suppression or PR include the ticket link and the forensic artifact hash for traceability. :mag:
